mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past three months signals an active monetary easing cycle, reducing discount rates on future corporate earnings and increasing the present value of equities, which drives positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of declining FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 9.0% over a one-month period signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which increases the probability of a near-term recession and triggers a flight to safety, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 9.0%, or the signal fails to generate negative returns in 70% of triggered cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: The joint signal of declining HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative SPX returns in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95.0 for two consecutive months indicates a contraction in real output, signaling a weakening economy and reducing corporate profitability, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during INDPRO contraction periods (t-test p > 0.05) or the signal's Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the CPIAUCSL above 215.0 within one month signals accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to delay rate cuts or initiate tightening, which increases real discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative after CPIAUCSL exceeds 215.0, or the signal's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in residential construction (HOUST) above 535.0 after two consecutive months of decline signals a recovery in housing demand, which acts as a leading indicator of broader economic expansion and drives positive S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the signal's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a labor market contraction, which reduces consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: The joint signal of declining PAYEMS and rising UNRATE fails to predict negative SPX returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption (RSAFS) below 340,000 million dollars for two consecutive months, combined with a stagnating GDP growth (GDPC1 < 11360.0), indicates a weakening demand environment that reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
